Title: Preflight inventory and reconciliation
User story / technical objective: Before writing code, inventory what already exists so IADM-05 reuses it and creates no duplicate platform.
Acceptance criteria: Report covers: working-tree state and branch; conventions used by IADM-01, IADM-02, IADM-04 (service layout, port, gateway prefix, permission-key naming, migration style, RLS and FORCE RLS style, request-context handling); the shared audit capability actually in use; shared identity and token claims; logging; frontend desk pattern. Anything not found is written as TBC, never guessed. Confirms DB target is the DEV Supabase project and not production.
Build default or status: Read-only; no code or DB change in this step

Title: IADM-05 service scaffold
User story / technical objective: Create IADM-05 as a separate deployable Java service following the conventions found in the preflight.
Acceptance criteria: Service starts, health endpoint answers, gateway route added using the same prefix and port convention as IADM-01/02/04; exception handling and structured logging in place; no sensitive payload in logs; technical doc started.
Build default or status: Port and route follow convention found in preflight; not hard-coded from memory

Title: Permission-key catalogue and role mapping
User story / technical objective: Define the IADM-05 permission keys and map them to the five roles that have an IADM-05 posture.
Acceptance criteria: Key catalogue follows the naming convention found in preflight. Mapping: R01 Super Admin = manage; R02 System Admin = write (propose/submit, never approve); R03 Institution Admin = view own institute only; R04 College Admin = view plus domain-workflow entry information only; R28 Auditor = view only. No wildcard key. No role from R05-R27 or R29-R39 gets any IADM-05 key. View does not imply export, execute, delete or approve. Test proves each denial.
Build default or status: R03 stays view-only (G-16 open); R04 has no trigger capability in this build (G-02 open)

Title: Schema, tenant scoping and row-level security
User story / technical objective: Create IADM-05 policy and governance-request metadata tables in the DEV database with tenant scoping and row-level security.
Acceptance criteria: Migration applied only after the target is positively verified as DEV. Policy and request metadata only: no copies of domain records or export payloads. Row-level security and FORCE row-level security on every table. Test: one institute cannot read another institute's rows; missing or mismatched tenant context fails closed. Rollback script included.
Build default or status: Physical schema is a build proposal; reported at S0 for the owner record

Title: Shared audit integration
User story / technical objective: Emit audit events for every material decision and privileged request through the existing shared audit capability.
Acceptance criteria: Uses the capability found in preflight; no second audit store. Event carries actor, action, scope, policy version, decision and outcome references, with no sensitive payload. If required audit cannot be guaranteed, the privileged action is refused (fail closed). Test covers audit-unavailable behaviour.
Build default or status: If preflight finds no reusable audit capability this is a blocker: stop and report

Actor / role: R01 Super Admin; R02 System Admin (view)
Title: View the classification catalogue
User story / technical objective: As an authorized platform actor, I can view the classification catalogue.
Acceptance criteria: Screen lists definitions with name, status, version, owner and effective dates. Only authorized scope visible. Catalogue shows seeded DEMO ONLY definitions, never an empty list. A role without the view key gets 403. No cross-tenant raw browsing.
Build default or status: Labels are DEMO ONLY / NOT LEGAL CLASSIFICATIONS (G-06 open)

Actor / role: R01 Super Admin; R02 System Admin
Title: Propose a classification revision
User story / technical objective: As an authorized policy owner, I can propose a classification revision.
Acceptance criteria: Draft is created as a new version; the published version is untouched. Required metadata validated: identifier, name, description, handling guidance, owner, effective dates. Audit event emitted. Screen allows the proposer to actually create and submit the draft for review.
Build default or status: None

Actor / role: R01 Super Admin (approver); R02 System Admin (proposer only)
Title: Approve or reject a policy revision
User story / technical objective: As an authorized reviewer, I can approve or reject a policy revision.
Acceptance criteria: Decision, actor, timestamp, version and rationale reference recorded. Approver must differ from the author. R02, R03, R04 and R28 cannot approve (403). Rejection requires a rationale reference. Applies to classification, retention and privacy/consent revisions.
Build default or status: BUILD DEFAULT, owner to confirm: approver = R01 only, different account from author

Actor / role: R01 Super Admin; R02 System Admin
Title: Define a retention rule
User story / technical objective: As a policy owner, I can define a retention rule for a domain and record category.
Acceptance criteria: Rule holds domain, record category, scope, trigger, rule reference, hold handling, review date, version and approving authority. Duration is stored as TBC unless the owner supplies one; no number is invented. Nothing is purged or touched in any domain service. Goes through the same draft, review, approve path.
Build default or status: Invoice retention (IADM-04) and college archive rule D1 (IADM-01) stay open (G-18); only placeholders

Actor / role: R01, R02, R03 as authorized; R28 read-only
Title: Inspect policy history
User story / technical objective: As an authorized actor, I can inspect policy history.
Acceptance criteria: All versions with decisions and audit references traceable. R01 and R02 see platform scope. R03 sees only published versions applicable to its own institute. R28 sees all in assigned scope, read-only. No mutation control shown to R28 or R03.
Build default or status: None

Title: Publish an approved classification or retention version
User story / technical objective: As an authorized policy actor, I can publish an approved classification or retention policy version.
Acceptance criteria: Only approved versions can be published; effective dates required; previous version becomes superseded, not deleted; published version immutable; audit event emitted; domain contract can resolve it afterwards.
Build default or status: Publisher = approver role default (R01); owner to confirm

Title: Policy lifecycle engine
User story / technical objective: One versioned lifecycle used by classification, retention and privacy/consent policies: draft, in review, approved, published, superseded.
Acceptance criteria: Published versions are immutable; a revision creates a new version and never overwrites. Author and approver must be different accounts. Each decision records actor, timestamp, version and rationale reference. Superseded versions stay readable. Applicable-version resolution returns exactly one version or none (none = fail closed).
Build default or status: Build default for approver: R01 Super Admin only (see US-003)

Title: Demo dataset (DEMO ONLY), grown each slice
User story / technical objective: Seed synthetic demo data so every screen shows real work from the first slice.
Acceptance criteria: Two institutes with distinct policy scopes; personas R01, R02, one R03 per institute, one R04 per college, one R28 (use only the test accounts the owner already created; do not invent emails). Sample classification and retention records marked DEMO ONLY with duration TBC. Each later slice adds its own seeded rows (export, erasure, sharing, consent). No real student, guardian, health or financial data. Seeds are idempotent and removable.
Build default or status: Slice S1 seeds classification and retention rows; S2 to S4 extend

Actor / role: R01 Super Admin; R02 System Admin (requester)
Title: Submit a governed export request
User story / technical objective: As an authorized actor, I can submit a governed export request.
Acceptance criteria: Captures purpose, data domain, fields, tenant scope, destination and applicable policy version. Cross-tenant scope needs R01 platform authority and a recorded purpose, else refused. No applicable policy means refused (fail closed). No export payload stored. R03 and R04 cannot submit here (R04 only via its domain workflow).
Build default or status: Requester roles are a build default (G-16 keeps R03 view-only)

Title: Approve or reject an export request
User story / technical objective: As an authorized reviewer, I can approve or reject an export request.
Acceptance criteria: Reviewer differs from requester. Approval is separate from execution: approved request is dispatched to the owning domain service through the domain contract with policy version and correlation id. View does not imply export. Demo shows one approved in-scope request and one denied cross-tenant request.
Build default or status: Approval roles are a build default; export destination safeguards stay TBC (G-07)

Actor / role: R01 Super Admin; R02 System Admin (operator)
Title: Identify failed or partial domain execution
User story / technical objective: As an operator, I can identify failed or partial domain execution.
Acceptance criteria: Operator screen lists requests with state, domain, correlation id and failure state, without payloads. Unresolved domains highlighted. Operator can re-dispatch only the unresolved domains; the action is idempotent.
Build default or status: None

Title: Resolve policy version and report an outcome
User story / technical objective: As a consuming domain service, I can resolve the applicable IADM-05 policy version and report an execution outcome.
Acceptance criteria: Resolve returns the one published version for the domain and scope, or no applicable policy (fail closed). Outcome report is idempotent by correlation id and traceable to policy version and scope. Domain re-authorization and execution stay with the domain owner.
Build default or status: Exercised by the simulator in demo

Title: Governance request state machine and idempotency
User story / technical objective: Common request engine for export, erasure and sharing requests.
Acceptance criteria: States: submitted, in review, approved, rejected, dispatched, in progress, completed, partially completed, failed. Correlation id on every request. Duplicate submit or retry returns the original request, never a second execution. Global completed is impossible while any required domain outcome is unresolved. Re-dispatch affects unresolved domains only.
Build default or status: State machine is a build proposal; reported at S2

Title: Domain contract endpoints
User story / technical objective: Versioned service-to-service endpoints that domain-owning services call to resolve policy, acknowledge a request and report an outcome.
Acceptance criteria: Authenticated service caller required; unknown or forged caller rejected. Trusted tenant context, not client-supplied. Request carries policy id, immutable policy version and correlation id. Outcomes: accepted, rejected, in progress, completed, partially completed. Reports contain references only, no record content. IADM-05 never calls into a domain database. Contract documented as versioned.
Build default or status: Real domain services are not wired in this build; each contract stays TBC per owner

Title: Domain execution simulator (DEMO ONLY)
User story / technical objective: A clearly labelled demo-only caller that plays two domain services so partial completion and failure can be demonstrated.
Acceptance criteria: Simulator is flagged DEMO ONLY in code, data and UI; it uses the real domain contract endpoints as a normal caller; it touches no real domain data; it can be disabled by a single setting; can simulate completed, rejected, pending and unavailable.
Build default or status: Same approach as the IADM-04 simulator values

Actor / role: R01 Super Admin; R02 System Admin (requester)
Title: Submit an erasure governance request
User story / technical objective: As an authorized actor, I can submit an erasure governance request.
Acceptance criteria: Request holds an opaque subject reference and selected source domains; no personal data copied into IADM-05. Routed as pending to each owning domain through the domain contract. IADM-05 deletes nothing anywhere.
Build default or status: Erasure eligibility and exceptions stay TBC (G-05)

Actor / role: R01 Super Admin; R02 System Admin
Title: See per-domain erasure outcomes
User story / technical objective: As an authorized reviewer, I can see per-domain erasure outcomes.
Acceptance criteria: Table shows each domain with its own status and receipt reference. Partial completion is shown as partial. Rejected shows the domain's reason code. Demo shows one completed and one pending domain.
Build default or status: None

Actor / role: R01 Super Admin (approver); R02 System Admin (submitter)
Title: Govern a data-sharing agreement
User story / technical objective: As an authorized policy owner, I can govern a data-sharing agreement.
Acceptance criteria: Agreement holds provider, consumer, data domains and fields, purpose, tenant scope, permitted operations, onward-sharing restriction, validity period and revocation conditions. Validity period is mandatory; no wildcard; default is deny. Legal basis field stores only an owner-approved reference or TBC. Approver differs from submitter.
Build default or status: Approver default R01 (G-15)

Title: Publish a privacy/consent policy version (gated)
User story / technical objective: As an authorized policy actor, I can publish an approved privacy/consent policy version.
Acceptance criteria: Drafting, review and approval work through the normal lifecycle. The publish action exists but is blocked by a legal gate that stays closed: screen and API show 'Blocked: awaiting children's-data legal check (D-RBAC-M17)'. Test proves publish is refused even for R01. This build contains no way to open the gate.
Build default or status: Stays gated until counsel finishes the legal check; owner opens it later by a separate change

Title: Suspend, revoke or record expiry of an agreement
User story / technical objective: As an authorized agreement owner, I can suspend, revoke or record expiry of a data-sharing agreement.
Acceptance criteria: Statuses: active, suspended, revoked, expired. Changes are versioned and audited. Expiry is applied automatically at the validity end. Provider and consumer services can read the current status through the domain contract. Enforcement inside those services is outside this build.
Build default or status: Enforcement contract TBC (G-08)

Actor / role: R01, R02; R03 own institute; R28 read-only
Title: View retention, consent and sharing registers
User story / technical objective: As an authorized actor, I can view the retention, privacy/consent and data-sharing registers.
Acceptance criteria: Each register shows only records within the actor's scope. Seeded demo rows present in all three. Out-of-scope records return nothing, not an error that leaks existence.
Build default or status: None

Title: Close an erasure request
User story / technical objective: As an authorized reviewer, I can close an erasure request only when owner-approved closure criteria are met.
Acceptance criteria: Closure is blocked with a clear message while any required domain outcome is unresolved. Closure permitted only when every required domain is in a final state (completed, or rejected with recorded reason). Does not claim anything about personal data inside existing audit entries.
Build default or status: BUILD DEFAULT technical rule only; owner-approved closure criteria still TBC (G-05)

Title: View own-institute policy adherence
User story / technical objective: As R03, I can view my institute's policy adherence.
Acceptance criteria: View-only screen. Shows the published policy versions applicable to the institute and the status of that institute's own governance requests and domain outcomes. No other institute's data (test with a second institute). No write control shown or accepted by the API.
Build default or status: ASSUMPTION: adherence content is defined here as above because the blueprint does not define it; owner may adjust. Writes stay TBC (G-16)

Title: View applicable policy and domain-workflow entry points
User story / technical objective: As R04, I can view applicable policy and enter permitted domain workflows.
Acceptance criteria: Screen shows applicable published policy for the college's institute and a read-only list describing the permitted domain-workflow entry points. No edit or override control; direct API write returns 403. IADM-05 itself triggers no domain execution.
Build default or status: Exact R04 trigger capability TBC (G-02); entry points are informational only

Title: View governance evidence (read-only)
User story / technical objective: As R28 Auditor, I can view authorized governance evidence.
Acceptance criteria: Policy versions, decisions, request and receipt references and audit references in the assigned scope are visible. Every write or approve attempt returns 403. No audit administration function exposed.
Build default or status: None

Title: Failure-handling and isolation test suite
User story / technical objective: Automated tests for every row of the blueprint failure table and for tenant isolation.
Acceptance criteria: Covers: missing or invalid tenant context, no applicable policy, conflicting policy versions, domain unavailable (request stays pending), domain rejects, partial completion, approval or identity unavailable, audit unavailable (privileged action refused), duplicate request, expired or revoked policy. Plus role-boundary tests for R01, R02, R03, R04, R28 and one role from R05-R39 that must be denied. Log-leak check shows no sensitive payload or credentials in logs.
Build default or status: None

Title: Evidence pack and close-out
User story / technical objective: Prove the work is done the way the owner defined done.
Acceptance criteria: Headed run for each persona (R01, R02, R03, R04, R28) showing real work on every screen with seeded rows; test results; plain-language report; blueprint verification checklist ticked item by item with evidence; list of parked items and open gaps (G-01 to G-18) with what this build assumed. IADM-04 style partial markers only if something is truly incomplete.
Build default or status: None
